title: CaduceusCore NPU Hardware/Software ABI Schema
description: Single authoritative source for MMIO registers, opcodes, descriptor layouts, ring buffers, and capability bits. All generated bindings derive from this file.

compatibility.major_break: Any register offset change, opcode value renumbering, address region remapping, descriptor field reordering, ring layout change, or capability bit reassignment.
compatibility.minor_add: New registers in reserved offsets, new opcodes in unused value slots, new descriptor fields at end of layout, new capability bits, new address regions in previously reserved space.

abi.description: CaduceusCore NPU ABI version 1.0 — RTL Phase 3 SoC integration baseline.

BOOT_ROM.description: Ibex reset vector + firmware boot ROM (64 KB)

SRAM.description: NPU unified compute buffer SRAM (4 MB)

DOORBELL.description: Host↔NPU doorbell ring buffer control (4 KB)

DRAM.description: Host DDR DRAM data space (2 GB)

MXU.description: Matrix Multiply Unit — INT4×INT8→INT32, 64×64 broadcast MAC array with tile iterator.

BIAS_ADDR.description: Bias SRAM byte address (0 = no bias)

SCALE_ADDR.description: Scale SRAM byte address (0 = no scale)

SFU.description: Special Function Unit — 7 FP16 operators (Softmax, LayerNorm, GELU, ReLU, SiLU, RoPE, RMSNorm).

VECTOR.description: Vector Engine — 128-wide INT32 SIMD with 6 operators (ADD, MUL, MAX, SUM_REDUCE, CONV_F32, RESID_ADD).

B_ADDR.description: Operand B SRAM byte address (unused for unary ops)

DMA.description: Direct Memory Access — axi_cdma engine with 2 channels (ch0: DRAM→SRAM load, ch1: SRAM→DRAM store) and descriptor chain mode.

PCIE_DMA.description: PCIe DMA Engine — host↔NPU data transfer over PCIe Gen4 x4.
PCIE_DMA.note: sizeof(npu_pcie_dma_t) == 36 bytes; doorbell descriptor path uses first 8 registers (32 bytes). RD_ERR_CODE and WR_ERR_CODE are status/debug registers.

DOORBELL.description: Host↔NPU doorbell — ring buffer head/tail pointers and completion status.

notes.KNOWN_DISCREPANCY: COMPLETION_STATUS is declared as 16 entries (64 bytes at offset 0x14) in both regmap.py and npu-regmap.h, but firmware accesses COMPLETION_STATUS[cmd_id] where cmd_id can range up to RING_ENTRIES-1 (1023). This means writes for cmd_id >= 16 overflow the declared register window. The current RTL doorbell.v implements only a single LAST_STATUS register at offset 0x10 and no COMPLETION_STATUS array. This discrepancy must be resolved in a future ABI revision.

HOST_TAIL.description: Host writes after appending command entries; triggers NPU wakeup

NPU_TAIL.description: Host updates → NPU sees new commands

LAST_STATUS.description: Last command status (0=done, non-zero=error). Used by firmware for debug tracking.

COMPLETION_STATUS.description: Per-ring-index completion status array. WARNING: array_size=16 per ABI declaration; firmware indexes up to RING_ENTRIES (1024).

opcodes.description: Engine-level opcodes used by the firmware command dispatch table (dispatch_cmd() in npu_firmware.c). These are the Host-side command ring opcodes, not the ISA instruction opcodes.

isa_opcodes.description: NPU Instruction Set Architecture opcodes (5-bit field). Used by the CISC-style 32-bit fixed-length instruction encoder/decoder in sim/engine/isa.py.

descriptors.description: Descriptor layouts for each engine operation type. Field offsets are byte offsets from the descriptor base address in DRAM. All descriptors are little-endian packed uint32 arrays.

notes: Firmware reads: src[0]=input_addr, src[2]=output_addr, src[8]=dim, src[9]=pos, src[10]=sfu_op.
Firmware hardcodes input_sram=0x00000000, output_sram=0x00018000, ignoring descriptor fields [4]/[5].
Python spike_host writes valid SRAM values at [4]/[5] but firmware ignores them — known design inconsistency.

fields.name: input_sram
fields.description: SRAM input (firmware ignores, uses hardcoded value)

fields.name: output_sram
fields.description: SRAM output (firmware ignores, uses hardcoded value)

notes: Uses 6-word descriptor (24 bytes) — smaller than the 15-word generic layout.

command.description: Command ring entries (cmd_entry_t). Firmware reads opcode, desc_addr, flags from ring buffer in DRAM.

completion.description: Completion ring entries (completion_t). Firmware writes completion status after each command.

configuration.description: Firmware ring buffer configuration. Ring buffer starts at DRAM_BASE (0x80000000). Completion ring follows immediately after the command ring (ring_entries × cmd_entry_size bytes). tile_scale_bytes is the per-tile FP32 scale buffer size used by the firmware MMUL path (64 columns × 4 bytes); the Python tile_scheduler intentionally uses a wider 128-column grouping (512B).

status_codes.description: Standard completion status codes. Non-zero values indicate error conditions.

capability_bits.description: Device capability bitmask. Read by host during device discovery.

sfu_sub_opcodes.description: SFU hardware control register OP field values (SFU.CTRL [3:0]).

vector_sub_opcodes.description: Vector hardware control register OP field values (VECTOR.CTRL [3:0]).

INT4xINT8.description: INT4 weights × INT8 activations → INT32 accumulation

INT8xINT8.description: INT8 weights × INT8 activations → INT32 accumulation

known_discrepancies.description: Known contract discrepancies across Python/C/RTL that will be resolved in future ABI revisions.

items.description: DOORBELL.COMPLETION_STATUS declared as 16 entries (offset 0x14, 64 bytes) in both regmap.py and npu-regmap.h. Firmware writes COMPLETION_STATUS[cmd_id] where cmd_id ranges up to RING_ENTRIES-1 (1023). RTL doorbell.v implements only LAST_STATUS at 0x10 and no COMPLETION_STATUS array. Resolution: define HW doorbell window vs firmware SRAM-backed completion array as separate concepts, or expand the hardware register window.

SFU firmware read_sfu_desc() hardcodes input_sram=0x00000000, output_sram=0x00018000, ignoring descriptor fields [4]/[5]. Python spike_host writes valid SRAM values at these offsets. This is a design inconsistency — firmware should either use descriptor SRAM fields or the descriptor layout should document them as firmware-ignored.

SFU read_sfu_desc() hardcodes pos=0 for non-ROPE ops. The descriptor field at offset 9 is only used by ROPE dispatch. For current forward passes (pos=0), this is correct but not architecturally clean.

sizeof(npu_pcie_dma_t) == 36 bytes (9 registers), but doorbell descriptor path uses only first 8 registers (32 bytes). RD_ERR_CODE and WR_ERR_CODE at offsets 0x1C/0x20 are status/debug registers outside the descriptor budget.
